CORPORATE 
 
The Corporate Franchise Team is diligently 
working on updating Kilkenny's electoral register 
following the commencement of the new Rolling 
Register and in anticipation of the local and 
European Elections.  This essential task is aimed 
at enhancing the accuracy of our Electoral 
Register. 
 
However, we cannot accomplish this crucial task 
without the active participation of the citizens of 
Kilkenny. Whether you are already registered or 
not, each and everyone plays a vital role in this 
process. We are requesting people’s assistance in 
verifying and, if necessary, updating their voter 
information. By including details such as your 
date of birth and PPSN, this contributes to the 
verification process, enhancing the integrity of 
our electoral system. 
 
Furthermore, we encourage people to inform us 
of any necessary changes, such as the removal of 
deceased family members from the register. We 
understand how distressing it can be to receive a 
polling card for a loved one who is no longer with 
us.  The Elected Members’ assistance in raising 
awareness 
about 
this 
initiative 
is 
greatly 
appreciated.

Reduce-Your-Use Campaign 
Kilkenny County Council is now three months into the national Reduce Your Use campaign, which will 
conclude in March 2024. An information landing page has been set up on the Kilkenny County Council 
website to inform staff on ways to reduce their energy use within the organisation, including video, tips 
and facts. See Information Page   
 
As part of the campaign we have selected the Callan and Thomastown Area Offices as case studies and we 
have implemented a number of energy-saving initiatives that will help us reach our energy saving targets 
of at least 15%.  A report on the final results will be completed and presented on completion of the campaign. 
 
Climate Action Promotional Campaign (HVO Trial) 
Kilkenny County Council’s Climate Action Team’s ongoing promotion through the use of videos, have over 
the last few weeks included a promo on Kilkenny County Council Climate Action activities and the recently 
announced Climate Action Community Grant. A third video promo has been completed and promoted in  
January. This promo was completed in partnership with the Kilkenny County Council machinery yard and 
focuses on Kilkenny County Council’s test use of HVO (Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil) in some of our diesel-
powered vehicles. HVO is a replacement fuel for diesel, made from recycled vegetable oil and can reduce 
emissions by up 90%.  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HJpiC87N_KY&t=20s 
 
These Climate Action video promos are uploaded on our newly developed Climate Action website and will 
play a key role in helping us communicate with the wider community. The videos are also being promoted 
on social media, with one of the Climate Action videos recently posted having over 10,000 
views/impressions on Facebook.   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
National Climate Action Plan 2024 
The Government approved the 2024 National Climate Action Plan on 20th December last. Public 
consultation on the Plan will take place shortly. The Plan builds on the Climate Action Plan 2023 and 
outlines how Ireland will accelerate the actions required to respond to the climate crisis, putting climate 
solutions at the centre of Ireland’s social and economic development. For more details see 
https://www.gov.ie/en/press-release/fcf90-government-approves-climate-action-plan-2024-for-public-consultation/ 
 
Environment Complaints 
All Environmental complaints received are logged on the CRM (Customer Relations Management) 
System.  The number of complaints that have been received and logged by Environment staff for 
investigation in January 2024 was 102, compared with 101 for January 2023 (i.e. a small increase of 1%).  The 
nature of these complaints ranged from littering, illegal dumping, burning of waste and abandoned 
cars.  The majority continue to be related to littering and illegal dumping.  Whilst every effort is made to 
bring unacceptable environmental practice into compliance, Environment Enforcement staff continue to 
manage significant enforcement cases progressing through prosecution cases.

Litter Management Plan 
A draft Litter Management Plan 2024-2026 is now in place. See the below timeline for the remainder of the 
process. 
 
The draft plan was brought before SPC 4 on the 7th of February last, and will be going live on consult.ie on 
Monday 19th of February for a 4 week public consultation period. 
 
Green Schools 
The Environmental Awareness Officer (EAO) continues to support 92 schools as part of the An Taisce Green 
Schools Programme to renew or attain a flag. Green schools is an international environmental education 
programme, offering a well-defined, controllable way for schools to take environmental issues into the 
curriculum and apply them to the day-to-day running of the school. Green schools is a holistic, long-term 
programme and has a two-year cycle in relation to preparation, assessment and attainment of a particular 
flag. 
 
The EAO is continuing to assist schools around the County to renew their membership as part of the Green 
Schools programme under their respective themes- Litter and Waste, Energy, Water, Travel, Biodiversity 
and Global Citizenship. Deadline for the applications for School Flags is March 15th, 2024. The EAO has 
assessed 6 schools for their application for a Green Flag since the 1st of February.

The Council co-funded a new biodiversity awareness programme with Keep Kilkenny Beautiful (KKB) 
called “Nature Nurture”. Members of the KKB committee and the EAO are visiting registered schools who

biodiversity friendly. The pupils are being presented with a specially commissioned “Biodiversity in your 
Garden” colouring book (which was illustrated by a local Kilkenny artist), pencils and native plants. The school 
has to complete their proposed actions within 6 months of taking the pledge. 
 
School Mobility Management Teams for Sustainable Transportation Initiatives 
As part of our ongoing commitment to promoting sustainable transport and fostering a healthier, more 
active lifestyle among students, Kilkenny County Council invited secondary schools within the City to 
participate in a schools mobility management initiative. 
 
Schools were invited on the 31st of January, 2024 to set up Mobility Management Teams comprised of 5 to 
6 enthusiastic transition year students, and are supported by Kilkenny County Council to implement 
initiatives aimed at encouraging walking, cycling, and park-and-stride practices with the aim of creating a 
positive impact on both the environment and the overall well-being of our community. The following 
Schools are participating so far: 
 
▪

Key objectives of the Mobility Management Teams: 
 
▪ 
Promote Walking: Encourage students to adopt walking as a primary mode of transport to and from 
school. 
▪ 
Embrace Cycling: Advocate for cycling as a sustainable and healthy alternative for daily commuting. 
▪ 
Park-and-Stride Initiatives: Collaborate on encouraging parents to park their vehicles away from the 
school entrance and encourage students to walk the remaining distance to school. 
 
The initiative is being supported by 4 departments within Kilkenny Local Authority: Planning, 
Environment, Health and Active Travel. 
 
 
The Deposit Return Scheme 
This is a new bottle and can recycling system known as the Deposit Return Scheme. The scheme began on 
1st February 2024. The cost of the deposit is automatically added to the cost of the drink. You can reclaim 
the deposit by returning your containers and participating outlets with a Reverse Vending Machine (RVM), 
once they are empty and undamaged. This includes bottles, tins and cans made from plastic, steel and 
aluminum between 150ml and 3 litres.

7 
 
No glass, dairy products or containers over 3 litres will be accepted. Containers between 150ml and 500ml 
will have a 15c deposit. Containers between 500ml and 3 litres will have a 25c deposit. 
 
You can return containers to shops that have a Reverse Vending Machine (RVM) or accept the containers 
manually. Some shops have a takeback exemption as they are not able to accept the containers back for the 
Deposit Return Scheme. There is an interactive map online on www.re- turn.ie to establish stores that are 
participating. 
 
WASTE 
 
Waste Enforcement 
Kilkenny County Council have begun compiling their data for the RMCEI return due on 29th February. 
This data includes an inspection of our 41 licensed sites across the County. In 2023, 61 enforcement files 
were opened for unauthorised sites against individuals and companies during the year. Some files were 
closed when a satisfactory environmental outcome was achieved. Other files remained open with the 
potential for these to be brought forward for criminal prosecution in 2024. Kilkenny County Council has 
been asked by the EPA to present at the National Waste Conference in March 2024 to share their experiences 
on enforcement cases. 
 
Bring Banks Usage 
The Council provides and manages 46 Bring Centres across the City and County.  A total of 198 tonnes of 
recyclables were collected from our Bring Centres so far in 2024.  This represents that the 1% increased to 
the prior year during the same period. Loughboy shopping centre (18 tonnes collected), Aldi Kilkenny city 
(16 tonnes collected) and New Park Shopping centre (13 tonnes collected) are the busiest locations in the 
City and Aldi, Ferrybank (8 tonnes collected) is the busiest outside of the city.  Environment staff are 
continuing to work very closely with our service providers to ensure the collection service is in keeping 
with demand, especially around long weekends and holiday periods. 
 
Dunmore Civic Amenity Site (CAS) 
Our site at Dunmore continues to be one of the busiest amenity sites in the country. During 2023 we have 
seen an increase in the volumes of material delivered to the site when compared to 2022. In 2023 the 
Dunmore CAS received 1786 tonnes of Municipal Solid Waste and 973 tonnes of Municipal Dry Waste. 
 
National Brown Bin Collection Scheme 
From January 2024, new legislation means every household will be entitled to avail of a brown bin collection 
service. Approximately 69% of households in Ireland up until now, are able to avail of a food waste 
collection service from their waste service collector. MyWaste.ie is encouraging everyone, here, there, and 
everywhere to contact their waste collector and request a brown bin service in 2024, because “you’re never 
too remote to recycle!” (Details https://www.mywaste.ie/brown-bin-service/).

CCTV 
On 13th December last, three draft Codes of Practice were submitted to Ossian Smyth TD, Minister of State 
with Special Responsibility for Public Procurement, eGovernment, Communications and the Circular 
Economy: 
 
(i) 
Draft Code of Practice on the operation of CCTV under the Waste Management Act 1996 (as 
amended);  
 
(ii) 
Draft Code of Practice on the operation of CCTV under the Litter Pollution Act 1997 (as amended); 
and 
 
(iii) 
Draft Code of Practice on the operation of Mobile Recording Devices under the Waste Management 
Act 1996 (as amended). 
 
Codes have now been approved by the Minister and have been laid before the Houses of the Oireachtas in 
accordance with Sections 22 and 33 of the Circular Economy and Miscellaneous Provisions Act 2022.  We 
now await commencement of the legislation which has to be completed by the Attorney General’s Office 
and the Department of the Environment, Climate and Communications shortly. Whilst awaiting the 
commencement order, the Local Authority Waste Programme Coordination Office is overseeing the 
development of the standardised operating procedures and procedural templates that need to be in place 
before CCTVs and MRDs can be put in to practice. This is required in advance of turning back on any 
cameras at bottlebanks etc. In accordance with Section 12 of the Code of Practice, the Environment section 
is presently preparing Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs), identifying sites, associated risks, 
signage, etc. 
 
AIR NOISE WATER 
 
Domestic Waste Water Treatment System Inspections 2023 
Under the National Inspection Plan for Domestic Wastewater Treatment Systems 2022-2026 the 
Environment Section of Kilkenny County Council has carried out 51 inspections in total. Out of the 51 
inspections 28 Wastewater Treatment Systems Passed. 19 Wastewater Treatment Systems Failed and a 
further 4 need a follow up inspection. From the 1st of January 2024 the septic tank grant will increase from 
€5,000 to €12,000. In order to apply for the grant all homeowners must have their septic tank registered, and 
will either have to be inspected by the Local Authority under the National Inspection Plan or be located in 
a Prioritised Area for Action or High-Status Objective Area.

Discharge License’s – Trade Effluents 
Currently the Environment Section along with external consultants are reviewing all 25 Discharge licenses 
in the County Kilkenny. Discharge licences are issued under Section 4 of the Local Government (Water 
Pollution) Act 1977, as amended in 1990, in respect of the discharge of trade effluent to surface water or 
groundwater. Licences set conditions so the discharge is treated and controlled in a manner that protects 
the receiving environment.

The Community Monuments Fund has 3 Streams: 
 
Stream 1 will offer grants up to €100,000 aimed at essential repairs and capital works for the conservation 
and repair of archaeological monuments. 
 
Stream 2 will offer grants of up to €30,000 for development of Conservation Management Plans/Reports 
that are aimed at identifying measures for conservation of archaeological monuments and improving public 
access. 
 
Stream 3 will offer grants of up to €30,000 for enhancement of access infrastructure and interpretation 
(including virtual/online) at archaeological monuments.

arm Inspections 
The Environment Section of Kilkenny County Council are currently issuing correspondence to all 82 
farmers who had Farm Inspections carried out by the Environment Section of Kilkenny County Council in 
2023 under the European Union (Good Agricultural Practice for Protection of Waters) Regulations 2022. 
The farm inspections were out in mainly the Nuenna and Dinin Catchments in the north of the county with 
a small number farm in other catchments selected.  
 
Out of the 82 farms inspected a compliance rate of 30% was achieved with the European Union (Good 
Agricultural Practice for Protection of Waters) Regulations 2022. 32% of farmers were issued an advisory 
letter with 27% issued a warning letter for non-compliances with the regulations. The remaining 12% were 
cross reported to the Department of Agricultural, Food & the Marine for non-compliance with the European 
Union (Good Agricultural Practice for Protection of Waters) Regulations 2022.  The Environment Section is 
in the process of selecting farms for inspection in 2024.

Woodstock House (Ruin) 
Woodstock House is currently in very poor condition and will continue to deteriorate without intervention. 
The increased frequency of heavy rainfall events resulting from global warming will accelerate this 
deterioration.  In response to the above, an application for funding to secure the ruin was submitted recently 
under the Historic Structures Fund.  
 
The proposed works under this phase concentrate on securing the ruin for the long term. The scope of the 
works include the removal of the significant vegetation and thereafter focus on stabilising the main front 
and rear elevations. This work when complete will allow for surveying and assessment of the interior fragile 
walls with a view to preparing a future repair plan for same.

Conservation 
The Conservation Office manages all protected 
structures in Kilkenny County and City. These 
structures are recognised for the following special 
interest: Architectural, Historical, Archaeological, 
Artistic, Cultural, Scientific, Technical, Social. 
 
An advisory service on conservation matters is 
provided to the public and colleagues, while the 
conservation grants and funding applications are 
also delivered.  
 
Applications have been received for the Built 
Heritage Investment Scheme (18 in total) and the 
Historic Structures Fund (5 in total).  
 
Built Heritage Investment Scheme (BHIS) 2024 
The aim of the Built Heritage Investment Scheme 
is to investment in a significant number of small-
scale, labour-intensive conservation projects 
throughout the county and to support the 
employment 
of 
conservation 
professionals, 
craftspeople and tradespersons in the repair of the 
historic built environment. Kilkenny’s grant 
allocation 
is 
€156,800, 
with 
a 
further 
supplementary finding of €22,950 ring fenced for 
thatched structures.   
 
Historic Structures Fund (HSF) 2024 
Funding for the Historic Structures Fund (HSF) is 
being made available as part of Project Ireland 
2040. The primary focus of the Historic Structures 
Fund will be on conservation and enhancement of 
historic structures and buildings for the broader 
benefit of communities and the public. 
 
Stream 1 will offer grants from €15,000 up to 
€50,000 and is aimed at essential repairs and 
smaller capital works for the refurbishment and 
conservation of heritage structures.

shopfronts, each Local Authority is invited to 
submit an additional application under Stream 1 
for eligible essential repairs and small capital

associated details to safeguard them and keep 
them in use.

additional 
application 
for 
Irish-language

€50,000 up to €200,000 for larger enhancement, 
refurbishment 
or 
reuse 
projects 
involving 
heritage structures, where:

projects 
must be

by the applicant in relation to the significance of 
the project and the works proposed.

Living Tradition: A Strategy to Enhance the 
Understanding, Minding and Handing on of Our

vernacular structures that are not listed in local 
authority Records of Protected Structures or 
otherwise legally protected.

The Tenant (Incremental) Purchase Scheme 2016, which allows local authority tenants to buy their 
homes is being revised as of from 29th January, 2024.  Changes to the scheme are as follows: 
 
▪ 
Minimum Income Requirements: The minimum income required for an applicant to be eligible to 
apply under the scheme has been revised from €12,500 to €11,000 per annum. (At least 50% of which 
must come from a reckonable primary source of income).

26 
 
▪ 
Primary Sources of Income: In addition to employment and the State Pension (Contributory and Non-
Contributory) being considered as primary sources of income, the Widow’s, Widower’s, Surviving 
Civil Partner’s (Contributory and Non-Contributory Pension), Blind Pension, Invalidity Pension and 
Disability Allowance are now also considered primary sources of income. 
 
▪ 
Time Receiving Social Housing Supports: The period of time tenants will be required to be in receipt 
of social housing support to be considered eligible under the scheme remains at 10 consecutive 
years. However, in the case of joint tenancies only one tenant is now required to have been in receipt 
of social housing supports for 10 years. 
 
▪ 
Income Included/Not Included as a Secondary Income for Assessment:  Changes have been made 
to income that can be considered and not considered as secondary income when assessing for 
discount.

The Affordable Housing Team are continuing to prepare for the roll out of this scheme.   
Under the Local Authority Affordable Purchase Scheme, Kilkenny County Council will make homes 
available at a reduced price for eligible applicants who are seeking to purchase a newly built home but 
need additional funds to bridge the gap between their mortgage and deposit to cover the full price of 
the home.  In return, Kilkenny County Council will take a percentage Equity Share in the Affordable 
Home.  Purchasers will enter into an Affordable Dwelling Purchase Agreement with Kilkenny County 
Council.   The purchaser can redeem or ‘buy out’ this Equity Share at a time of their choosing but there 
is no obligation to do so. If the purchaser chooses not to redeem the Equity Share while living in the 
home, the Council can do so when the property is sold, transferred or after the death of the owner. 
 
For more details on the Local Authority Affordable Purchase Scheme please check out the Kilkenny 
County Council Information Webpage at  
https://www.kilkennycoco.ie/eng/services/housing/local-authority-affordable-purchase-scheme/ 
 
It is advisable that those interested in the scheme review the information carefully where they will find 
general information on the scheme along with eligibility criteria, how to apply, the documentation 
required to accompany an application etc.  Inquiries to affordablehousing@kilkennycoco.ie  
 
VACANT HOMES 
The Vacant Properties Refurbishment Grant, Croí Cónaithe is one of the measures in order to address 
vacancy and efficient use of existing stock in Housing for All.  The grant is aimed at bringing vacant 
and derelict properties back into residential use.  The scheme was originally for people who were 
refurbishing vacant properties for use as their principal private residence.  The Government has 
recently announced that as of 1st May 2023, there will be a number of changes to this scheme including 
that the scheme will be expanded to property owners who wish to refurbish their vacant property for 
rental purposes.  The detail and guidance regarding the modified scheme have not yet been issued by 
the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage.   There has been a substantial increase in 
the number of calls to the Housing Department regarding this scheme and a Register of all inquiries to 
the Council will be kept for follow up when further details of the revised scheme are available. 
 
All queries in relation to this grant should be submitted by email to vacanthomes@Kilkennycoco.ie and 
will be responded to.

Local Government Rates & Other Matters Act 2019 
Following the enactment of the Local Government Rates and other Matters Act the following important 
changes have come into effect. 
 
Payment of Commercial Rates 
In previous years, Commercial Rates were payable in two moieties, with the first 50% (plus any arrears 
due) being due on issue of the demand, and the second 50% falling due on the 1st of July. Commercial 
Rates are now payable in full from 1st January 2024.

32 
 
 
 
Change of Occupant/Owner 
It is the duty of a ratepayer to inform a local authority where they: 
 
(i) 
cease to be a liable person, 
(ii) 
become a liable person, 
(iii) 
change their status as a liable person. 
 
The penalty for contravening this requirement, without reasonable excuse, is being guilty of an offence 
and being liable, on summary conviction, to a Class A fine.  
 
A liable person is: 
 
(i) 
the occupier of the relevant property on the first day of the local financial year; 
 
(ii) 
if the relevant property is unoccupied on that day, the person who is for the time being entitled 
to occupy the property on that day.  
 
Payment of Rates on Sale of Relevant Property 
A liable person who proposes to sell a relevant property is required to pay to the local authority any 
rates and accrued interest which is due and payable in respect of that property in their capacity as a liable 
person on or before the completion of the sale.  
Unpaid rates and interest will be a charge on relevant property.  
 
Valuation List 
Amendments to a valuation list will be effective immediately i.e. revisions, additions and removals and 
appeals (Valuation Tribunal and Courts).  There will now be a provision for pro-rata liability and billing 
where occupation ends or begins mid-year. 
 
Incorrect Information 
There is a requirement to give notice within 10 days to the local authority if you become aware that 
incorrect information is being held by the local authority in respect of commercial rates. The penalty for 
contravening this requirement, without reasonable excuse, is being guilty of an offence and being liable, 
on summary conviction, to a Class A fine.
